title: NVLink fabric glitch: field scrapbook and triage notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick field notebook capturing raw on-call observations, commands run, and first-pass hypotheses for the recent NVLink/ECC flaps that led to several GPU driver crashes and a kernel panic on cluster-gpu-17. This is intentionally informal — use this to seed a formal postmortem and a focused runbook (separate doc).

Summary of the event (high level):
- Window: 2025-07-01 03:12–03:45 UTC (first alerts), recurring flaps through 2025-07-01 11:00 UTC.
- Impact: 5 training pods evicted across 3 nodes (cluster-gpu-12, cluster-gpu-17, cluster-gpu-21). One node (cluster-gpu-17) experienced a kernel panic and required a hard reboot.
- Observed signals: rising ECC single-bit counts on affected GPUs, NVLink peer-reset messages, nvidia driver oops leading to GPU timeout, then kernel panic on cluster-gpu-17 with machine check-like stack.

Initial evidence (raw snippets captured during triage):
- nvidia-smi -q -d ECC (after incident on cluster-gpu-12):
  GPU 0 ECC Single-bit: 183 -> 512 (in 2 hours)
  GPU 1 ECC Single-bit: 4 -> 6  (unchanged)
- dmesg (cluster-gpu-17 excerpt):
  [Jul 1 03:20:41] NVRM: GPU at 0000:86:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
  [Jul 1 03:20:41] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:86:00): 31, GPU has fallen off the bus
  [Jul 1 03:20:42] nvidia: probe of 0000:86:00.0 failed with error -110
  [Jul 1 03:21:03] nvlink0: nvlink fabric error: lane 2 severe parity
  [Jul 1 03:21:05] Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt

- /var/log/messages (snippet):
  Jul 01 03:21:03 cluster-gpu-17 kernel: nvlink0-2: link flapping detected, peer reset issued
  Jul 01 03:21:03 cluster-gpu-17 gpu-healthd[4321]: detected ECC spike GPU0: +329 sb, marking degraded

- ipmitool sel elist (no obvious chassis faults)

Triage steps performed (ordered roughly as executed):
1) Isolate node from serving: cordon + drain k8s node (evacuate pods). We did this for cluster-gpu-17 and cluster-gpu-12 after repeated errors.
2) Capture state: ran nvidia-bug-report.sh, collected /var/log/messages, dmesg, journalctl -k, and ipmitool SEL.
3) Query ECC counters: nvidia-smi -q -d ECC and nvml samples.
4) Check NVLink topology and peers: nvidia-smi topo -m, nvidia-smi nvlink -s. Observed transient missing peers on cluster-gpu-17 at times of flaps.
5) Attempt soft recovery: rmmod nvidia_uvm; rmmod nvidia; modprobe nvidia (note: modprobe sometimes failed after peer-reset). When soft recovery failed we performed controlled reboot.
6) Swap PCIe slot -> reseated GPU on cluster-gpu-12 (eng-facility assistance). Post-reseat ECC spikes subsided on that node for ~6 hours.

Hypotheses (ordered by likelihood from today's notes):
- Hypothesis A: Intermittent NVLink fabric hardware fault (connector/cable or GPU NVLink link) causing parity errors and generating ECC activity, eventually propagating to driver instability. Evidence: explicit nvlink parity messages, link flapping messages, hardware-seeming symptoms. Reseat improved one node.
- Hypothesis B: GPU firmware/BIOS microcode regression interacting poorly with NVLink on this vintage board. Evidence: similar fleet of nodes with same motherboard + GPU firmware versions clustered in affected set. No BIOS updates applied in last quarter.
- Hypothesis C: Driver bug triggered by repeated ECC/parity events (edge-case state machine). Evidence: driver oops + Xid 31 and subsequent timeouts. We have an open runtime PR to add protective checks (linked).
- Hypothesis D: Power/thermal transient causing ECC spikes and fabric flaps. Evidence: rack PDU logs show minor voltage sag at 03:18 on the rack powering cluster-gpu-17 (needs verification with power team).

Immediate mitigations used during incident: 
- Cordoned affected nodes (k8s) and drained workloads to spare capacity.
- Enabled aggressive eviction threshold for batch jobs in the cluster to prevent repeated thrash.
- In-flight failures caused us to shift latency-sensitive workloads to Dedicated pools to maintain customer SLOs.
- Reseated one GPU and observed temporary improvement.
- Collected nvidia-bug reports and uploaded to S3 for vendor debug (s3://redwood-debug/nvlink-2025-07-01/).

Draft runbook items (to refine into a separate, short checklist):
- Alerting thresholds: ECC single-bit > 100/hour OR NVLink parity messages > 5 in 10m => P2 alert to SRE on-call.
- Triage checklist (fast path):
  * Step 0: Acknowledge alert, check dashboards (ECC rates, NVLink parity counts, node health).
  * Step 1: If ECC spike + nvlink messages: cordon node and set unschedulable.
  * Step 2: Collect: nvidia-smi -q -d ECC, nvidia-smi topo -m, dmesg | tail -n 200, journalctl -k -b --no-pager > kernel.log, ipmitool sel elist. Archive with timestamped prefix.
  * Step 3: Try soft driver reload (only if node is drained and no critical pods): systemctl stop kubelet; rmmod nvidia_uvm; rmmod nvidia; modprobe nvidia. If rmmod hangs or fails, skip to reboot.
  * Step 4: If soft reload fails or errors persist: reboot node and monitor on boot for repeated nvlink messages. Mark node as quarantine for at least 24h after a kernel panic.
  * Step 5: If reseating is possible (data center on-site support): schedule reseat and test. Note: reseat requires maintenance window for clusters with stateful workloads.
  * Step 6: If repeated across nodes with same HW/firmware: open vendor case with NVidia and system vendor, attach bug reports (nvidia-bug-report) and dmesg, and request firmware/driver guidance.

Notes about safe operations and customer impact: 
- Avoid toggling ECC state in production unless instructed by vendor. Disabling ECC hides faults and risks silent data corruption.
- Do not run aggressive stress tests on production GPUs; use isolated maintenance nodes or lab cluster.

Telemetry gaps (follow-up list):
- Add NVLink parity/error counter export into metrics pipeline (we currently only scrape ECC and Xid counts).
- Per-GPU ECC rate alerting per hour and per-day.
- Dashboard tile for nvlink link-state transitions across the fleet.

Vendor and escalation plan (quick):
- File SRE-5321 (linked) with NVIDIA TAM + system vendor, include: nvidia-bug-report, nvlink messages, ECC counters, firmware versions, kernel version, driver version.
- If vendor requests further stress logs, prepare validated repro on an isolated spare node (run nvidia stress + synthetic nvlink stress if supported).

Action items (owners + suggested ETA):
- Evan: coordinate with onsite ops to RMA cluster-gpu-17 GPU if vendor confirms hardware fault. ETA 2025-07-14.
- Priya: add NVLink parity metrics to telemetry (exporter + dashboard). ETA 2025-07-09.
- Liam: run controlled firmware upgrade experiment on 1 spare rack and validate (coordinate with vendor). ETA 2025-07-20.
- Sofia (owner of doc): turn this field scrapbook into an official SRE postmortem + runbook doc. ETA 2025-07-12.

Open questions (raw and unresolved):
- Is the spike pattern correlated with specific workloads (memory-bound training jobs)? Need pod-level audit for the window.
- Did a rack-level power transient trigger the initial parity event? Request detailed PDU logs from infra.
- Are there BIOS/microcode versions that avoid this behavior? Vendor needs to confirm.

Useful commands and shortcuts (quick copy):
- Collect NV info: sudo nvidia-bug-report.sh --logfile /tmp/nvbug-$(date -Iseconds).tgz
- ECC counters: sudo nvidia-smi -q -d ECC | sed -n '1,120p' > /tmp/gpu-ecc-$(hostname).txt
- NVLink topology: sudo nvidia-smi topo -m > /tmp/topo-$(hostname).txt
- Recent dmesg: sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-$(hostname).log

Quick timeline (not exhaustive):
- 03:12 UTC: First ECC alert from cluster-gpu-12 (low priority)
- 03:18 UTC: NVLink parity messages start on cluster-gpu-17; driver Xid 31 observed shortly after
- 03:21 UTC: Kernel panic on cluster-gpu-17; node became unreachable; emergency reboot required
- 04:00–09:00 UTC: recurring nvlink parity messages seen on cluster-gpu-21 and cluster-gpu-12; evictions continued until we cordoned nodes and reseated one GPU

Appendix: candidate logs archived (S3):
- s3://redwood-debug/nvlink-2025-07-01/cluster-gpu-17-nvbug.tgz
- s3://redwood-debug/nvlink-2025-07-01/cluster-gpu-12-dmesg.log

If you're reading this and you were on call: add any missing snippets below (raw dmesg lines, any ssh session notes, quick impressions). We'll use this as the canonical raw-source for the PM-style postmortem.

-- Sofia M. (SRE)
